header.sector: Hyperscaler / cloud AI capital expenditure and the companies spending it
header.title: Hyperscaler AI capex surprises widen the range of S&P 500 earnings outcomes

s01_bottom_line.text: Largest US hyperscalers are on track to spend $800bn capex in 2026 (up 94%), with GS expecting $1.2tn in 2027 and $1.4tn in 2028; this capex flows into earnings of chipmakers, tech hardware, industrials and utilities and drives almost half of 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth. ⟨cited figures: approximate; forecast⟩

AI investment is a tailwind this year but is expected to fade to a marginal drag by 2028 as capex growth slows and depreciation rises; upside hinges on continued capex surprises. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩

The article names sectors benefiting from capex but does not quantify the per-company earnings or valuation impact for named suppliers; the thesis rests on capex continuing to surprise upward rather than decelerate.
